bull.b: Rapid growth in prescriptions, prescribers, and treated patients indicates that etripamil is gaining real-world adoption beyond initial testing. Emerging repeat use could support a more durable commercial base as physicians become familiar with the product and access improves.

Broader formulary coverage directly improves patient access and can reduce denials and co-pay support requirements. If maintained, this structural commercial progress should improve prescription conversion, average selling prices, and the efficiency of the company’s launch investment.

China’s approval is the first authorization outside the U.S. and gives Milestone an additional route to future revenue through an experienced regional partner. The milestone and royalty structure broadens etripamil’s commercial opportunity without requiring all international commercialization directly.

bear.b: The company’s current cost structure remains far ahead of its revenue base, so meaningful profitability depends on substantial future commercial growth. Persistent operating losses reduce financial resilience and make successful execution of the launch and pipeline essential to improving earnings power.

Large recurring cash outflows consume resources while product revenue remains early-stage, increasing dependence on available financing and future commercial progress. Even with runway into H2 2027, continued burn could constrain investment flexibility or require additional capital before self-sustaining cash generation.

Debt of roughly 3.3 times equity leaves a smaller balance-sheet buffer against ongoing losses and execution setbacks. The sharp decline in equity heightens financial risk and may limit the company’s flexibility to fund development and commercialization without further shareholder dilution.
